newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar falls sharply to 12-month low close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar falls sharply to 12-month low close.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished sharply lower against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday on an unconfirmed report that the central bank was pleased with the currency's steady recent depreciation, dealers said.
The dollar dipped as low as T$27.919 but recovered near the close to finish at T$27.880 against Tuesday's T$27.836 close.
The Taiwan dollar has not closed lower since finishing at T$27.892 exactly one year ago on May 28, 1996.
The Economic Daily News quoted an unidentified central bank official before the open as saying the bank was pleased by the "appropriate" recent depreciation as this would spur exports.
The central bank declined to comment on the report.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$447 million.
Dealers questioned the authenticity of the newspaper report, but said its effect in the market was palpable.
"The report, a strange one without clear sources, in effect forced importers and other investors to enter right from the opening to buy U.S. dollars," said one dealer.
The dealer said he believed the central bank had intervened in the last 15 minutes to prevent the Taiwan dollar from falling too sharply, although the close already was much lower than Tuesday's.
Dealers described investors as highly wary.
"Investors are still very cautious, with some taking immediate profits (by selling U.S. dollars)," one dealer said.
Dealers attributed the slow Taiwan dollar depreciation in part to the U.S. dollar's recent global appreciation.

Dealers said the local dollar also had tended lower due to persistent outflows of foreign equity funds and capital outflows triggered by recent political jitters over Taiwan's social order and ongoing constitutional reforms.
Caution over Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China on July 1 also fuelled some U.S. dollar demand, dealers said.

Dealers said they expected the downtrend to continue, with the dollar testing T$28 later in the year, though a wary central bank could be expected to monitor the situation closely -- and to act if the dollar sinks too quickly.
"The central bank likely would not allow more sharp falls by the Taiwan dollar," said one dealer.
For Thursday, a T$27.88-27.92 range was seen.
The last time the Taiwan dollar tested T$28 was one year ago after the central bank announced it was abandoning its decade-old level at T$27.5.
Because Taiwan's export-driven economy was recovering slowly at the time, the announcement was interpreted as a central bank green light for a depreciation that would spur exports.
-- James Peng (5080815)
